messages:
jordan: quick follow-up from the RFC review — a few edge cases popped up around chroot-per-component, signed indexes, and streaming verify on low-memory appliances. can we do a short sync on tradeoffs?

anika: short recap: current flow signs whole tarballs. agent verifies signature then extracts. problem: huge bundles on devices with <4GB free and multi-component deltas that touch separate partitions.

lee: if we adopt chroot-per-component (runtime, kernels, models) we can send smaller deltas and apply overlays per component. pro: lower peak RAM/IO. con: ordering gets tricky, and rollback semantics across components need careful spec.

miriam: hard constraint: many customer appliances only allow streaming download+verify. buffering complete artifact is a non-starter. propose index contains chunked SHA256 table so agent can hash-verify while streaming.

anika: minimal human-readable index sketch we discussed:
```
index.json
{
  \"version\": \"2026-03\",
  \"bundles\": [
    {\"name\":\"runtime\",\"size\":\"123456789\",\"sha256\":\"<root-hash>\",\"chunks\": [\"h1\",\"h2\", \"...\"]},
    {\"name\":\"kernels\",\"size\":\"987654\",\"sha256\":\"...\",\"chunks\": [\"...\"]}
  ],
  \"signer\": \"supply-chain-v1\"
}
```
Agent flow: download index -> verify index signature -> stream bundle, verify chunk hashes on the fly -> finalize root-hash. avoids buffering whole artifacts.

lee: chunk-table also lets us parallelize fetches from multiple mirrored proxies in airgapped setups. trade: index size and resume logic complexity go up.

jordan: key rotation: how do older agents validate new signing keys? we need a migration handshake or trusted-keys list baked into agent config.

miriam: handshake proposal: agent advertises capabilities + trusted key fingerprints. server replies with acceptable signing key(s) or fails. example snippet we discussed:
```
capabilities: [\"stream-verify\", \"chunked-apply\", \"swap-atomic\"]
trusted_keys: [\"sha256:abc123\"]
```
Agent rejects upgrade if no overlap unless operator override enabled.

anika: operator control: add an X-Verification-Mode header on index fetch (values: strict|fast). strict = verify index + chunks + bundle signatures; fast = verify index signature only. intended for maintenance windows on constrained gear.

lee: default must be strict. fast only via explicit agent config opt-in and logged. cannot be operator ad-hoc.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for offline-upgrade 2026-03-19T22:10Z -> 10% lab nodes :shipit:

miriam: apply/rollback pattern suggestion: dual-chroot-swap. write new components into /opt/redwood.new chroots, run health hooks, then atomically switch symlink /opt/redwood -> /opt/redwood.new. rollback = flip symlink back. caveat: ensure inodes and cleanup, and avoid IO storms when populating new chroots.

jordan: +1 to dual-chroot. add an orphan-cleaner lifecycle with rate limits to avoid IO spikes. include safety windows and backoff.

anika: action items: I'll draft RFC diff for index v2 (chunk table + signer metadata), handshake proto (capabilities + trusted_keys fingerprints), and an apply-plan object that server returns describing chroot ordering + health checks.

lee: signing granularity q: per-index vs per-bundle vs per-chunk signatures? per-chunk sigs blow up metadata size. per-index signed + chunk hashes seems like best tradeoff for constrained devices.

miriam: agree. chunk signatures are overkill for the typical appliance threat model; index signature + chunk hashes is sufficient and keeps transfer sizes reasonable.

jordan: next steps: anika posts RFC diff, miriam prototypes streaming verify with OpenSSL and measures memory/IO, lee drafts chroot overlay apply/rollback steps and failure modes. we'll reconvene after prototypes.

anika: aiming to post draft EOD tomorrow with operator examples and example curl header for X-Verification-Mode.

miriam: quick testing command that worked streaming without buffering:
```
# verify signature streaming with pubkey
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature bundle.sig < bundle.tar.gz
```
we piped it through and confirmed low memory footprint.

lee: add telemetry metrics: per-bundle verify_time, chunk_hash_failures, apply_swap_duration, orphan_cleanup_cycles. want alerts for repeated chunk failures to catch flaky storages.

jordan: great. keep this thread for RFC follow-ups. thanks everyone. :+1:
